title: Avondale Well Depth and Drilling Cost
meta_description: Avondale wells have a 41-foot median depth, 30 gpm median yield, and estimated finished-well costs of $7,400-$14,300.
h1: Avondale, Colorado Well Depth, Yield, and Cost
intro_html:
Avondale sits on the plains in Pueblo County, where permitted well records show generally shallow wells and strong reported yields. Within 5 miles of Avondale, Colorado DWR records include 1,904 wells, although only 985 are recorded as constructed. Of those, 969 report total depth, 71 report pump yield, and 66 report static water level.

That uneven reporting matters when you compare a property with nearby wells. The local records point to a shallow, productive setting, but a specific lot can still encounter poor material, a lower-producing interval, or a water-quality issue. Use neighboring permits as a starting point, not as a guarantee.

sections.heading: How deep are Avondale wells?
sections.html:
The median reported well depth around Avondale is 41 feet. The middle half runs from 32 to 50 feet, and 90% of reported wells are no deeper than 59 feet. The depth mix reinforces that pattern: 98% are under 100 feet, 1% fall between 100 and 300 feet, none are recorded between 300 and 600 feet, and 1% are 600 feet or deeper.

For a driller's bid, that means a typical Avondale hole is shallow, but the deepest record reaches 2,150 feet. The broad outlier range is a reminder that geology and the intended water source control the final design. Most permits name an unnamed or fractured-bedrock aquifer, while 55 name alluvial water. No Denver Basin aquifer wells appear in these records.

sections.heading: What Avondale wells produce
sections.html:
Reported pump yields are generally favorable. The median is 30.0 gallons per minute, with the middle half ranging from 15.0 to 367.5 gallons per minute. Eighty percent of the reported wells produce more than 15 gallons per minute. Seventeen percent fall between 5 and 15 gallons per minute, while 1% are between 1 and 5 gallons per minute and 1% are under 1 gallon per minute.

For a buyer, the small share under 1 gallon per minute is encouraging, but the sample is limited to 71 yield reports. A well's yield test is more useful than the neighborhood median. Ask for the completion report, pump test information, storage capacity, and any restrictions on the permit. An exempt household-use well also remains subject to Colorado rules, including the 35 gpm exempt-well pumping limit.

sections.heading: Avondale water levels and the reported trend
sections.html:
Reported static water levels are shallow. The median depth to water is 30 feet, and the middle half falls between 26 and 33 feet below the surface. That is useful when planning a pump setting, trenching, and electrical work, but it is not the same as a guaranteed water level on an untested lot.

The decade figures do not show a simple dropping water table in these records. The median measured water level was 32 feet below surface in the 2010s and 21 feet in the 2020s, meaning the later reported measurements were shallower. Only 66 wells report static water level, and measurement conditions vary, so treat this as a record-based signal rather than a basin-wide conclusion. Seasonal conditions, pumping, and well location can all affect a reading.

sections.heading: Who has drilled near Avondale, and when
sections.html:
Permit activity spans several generations. The records show 103 permits from the 1950s, 96 from the 1960s, 88 from the 1970s, 68 from the 1980s, 350 from the 1990s, 660 from the 2000s, 134 from the 2010s, and 60 from the 2020s. The newest permit year is 2025. A large share of the local inventory was permitted in the 1990s and 2000s, so many nearby wells may not represent current construction standards or current site conditions.

The most active names in the records are Authorized (Pe, Pg), with 585 wells; Lang Equipment, LLC (Lang, Alan F.), with 133; and Layne Western Company Inc. (Larson, Carl), with 93. Check the actual permit and completion documents rather than relying only on a driller name. DWR records can clarify use, construction, and reported performance.

sections.heading: What a new well costs in Avondale
sections.html:
For Avondale's alluvium and plains sedimentary rock, the drilling model uses a typical rate of $35-$55 per foot. At the local median depth of 41 feet, the drilled hole works out to about $1,400-$2,300. That is the hole only, not the complete water system.

A finished well with pump, pressure tank, trenching, and electrical is estimated at about $7,400-$14,300. A bid can move outside that range if the site needs unusual casing or grout, difficult access, extra trenching, treatment equipment, or a deeper-than-typical hole. Get the scope in writing and ask which items are included. Permit requirements, water rights, and an augmentation plan may also affect a proposed use in an over-appropriated basin.

sections.heading: Risks to check before buying or building
sections.html:
Low yield is not the main pattern in the reported Avondale data, but a buyer should still verify the individual well. The records include 1% under 1 gallon per minute and 1% between 1 and 5 gallons per minute, and many permits do not report a yield at all. Dry holes and poor production can occur even where neighboring wells perform well, especially where fractured material controls the water-bearing zone.

Water quality deserves separate attention. Within about 10 miles, the map includes 16 PFAS sampling or contamination sites and 7 EPA Superfund or cleanup sites. There are no historic mine features mapped in that area. Test an existing well for ordinary drinking-water concerns and site-specific contaminants, and inspect casing, grout, storage, and septic separation before relying on the water for a home.

sections.heading: A practical Avondale lot checklist
sections.html:
Before closing, pull the nearby permits and compare depth, use, yield, water level, aquifer description, and construction details. Boone is about 5 miles away, Vineland about 6 miles, Blende about 12 miles, Salt Creek about 13 miles, Pueblo about 14 miles, and Fowler about 19 miles; those places can provide broader context, but Avondale-area wells should carry the most weight.

For a build, confirm the well permit and intended use with Colorado DWR, locate the septic area, and leave room for access by a drilling rig and service truck. Plan for sampling before occupancy. If the property will add household demand, livestock, irrigation, or other uses, confirm that the permit allows it. A local contractor can also evaluate driveway access, trench routes, drainage, and the ground conditions that will affect the final bid.

faq.q: How deep are wells in Avondale, Colorado?
faq.a: The median reported well depth within 5 miles of Avondale is 41 feet. The middle half is 32 to 50 feet, and 98% of reported wells are under 100 feet. The deepest record is 2,150 feet, so a typical shallow estimate should not be treated as a guarantee for every lot.

faq.q: How much water do Avondale wells produce?
faq.a: Among the 71 wells reporting pump yield, the median is 30.0 gallons per minute. The middle half ranges from 15.0 to 367.5 gallons per minute, and 80% report more than 15 gallons per minute. Ask for the individual well's pump test because only a small portion of the records includes yield data.

faq.q: What does it cost to drill a well in Avondale?
faq.a: The local drilling model uses $35-$55 per foot. At Avondale's 41-foot median depth, the drilled hole is estimated at $1,400-$2,300. A finished system with pump, tank, trenching, and electrical is estimated at $7,400-$14,300. Access, casing, grout, deeper drilling, and site conditions can change the final bid.

faq.q: Is well water safe to drink in Avondale?
faq.a: A well permit does not establish that water is safe to drink. The mapped area includes 16 PFAS sampling or contamination sites and 7 EPA Superfund or cleanup sites within about 10 miles. Test an existing or new well before use, including for site-specific concerns. Review casing, grout, septic location, and the well's construction record.

faq.q: Is the water table dropping in Avondale?
faq.a: The available decade data does not show a straightforward decline. Median reported depth to water was 32 feet below surface in the 2010s and 21 feet in the 2020s, which is shallower in the later period. Only 66 wells report static water level, so the comparison is limited and does not prove a basin-wide trend.
